topics.label: Course introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the framing for the lecture by welcoming students, outlining learning objectives, and introducing the topic of cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: the interplay of intrinsic mutations, chance, and environmental exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental nature of cancer and explore how intrinsic cellular processes, stochastic mutations, inherited risks, and environmental factors interact across populations.

topics.label: Pathogen-driven carcinogenesis and the Burkitt lymphoma paradigm
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote cancer, using the specific discovery, epidemiology, and pathogenesis of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma as a primary model.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens: bioactivation, oxidative damage, and DNA adducts
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which chemical carcinogens and radiation undergo metabolic processing to induce DNA adducts, transversions, and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms in cancer development, focusing on how chronic inflammation, promotional signaling, and host developmental stages create permissive environments for tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Approaches for identifying mutational signatures and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen-induced mutational patterns and evaluate chemical safety.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing by summarizing the key themes of environmental cancer risks, testing challenges, and risk-benefit considerations.
